newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end sharply lower 2nd day in a row.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end sharply lower 2nd day in a row.

text.p: Lingering concern on the direction of the peso-dollar rate and high interest rates weighed down Philippine shares on Wednesday pushing the index below its support level at the close, traders said.
The main index ended sharply lower for the second straight session by 68.50 points, or 2.58 percent, at 2,587.36 points. It pierced through its 2,600 support.

"It's more of the same - high interest rates, uncertainty in the forex market. I think confidence was shaken and people, especially foreigners, are just waiting for the dust to settle," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development.
Turnover was 2.08 billion pesos, higher than the previous day's 1.84 billion.
"We are seeing more investors selling out for the simple reason that there's this uncertainty in the forex market," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities Inc.
"It's like we are trading blindly and the best position is maybe for investors to stay out of the market until there is a clearer direction," Ravelas added.
DBS Securities sales manager Bing Trinidad said high interest rates were sapping liquidity out of the equities market into higher yield fixed income instruments.
The Central Bank earlier raised interest rates to a 2 1/2 year high to defend the peso but has kept it unchanged despite assurances from bank officials that it will not stay high for long.
Losers trounced gainers 130 to 15 with 31 unchanged issues.
Index heavyweight issues Petron Corp, Metrobank, San Miguel Corp B and Meralco B continued to drag the index to lower levels. Gainers were mostly second and thirdliner issues.
Petron ended at its intra-day low of 5.70 pesos.
Both Arroyo and Ravelas said they expect the market to give in to minimal gains in the next few days after its sharp losses the past two sessions.
Traders pegged the next initial support at 2,570. Others said they were looking at the market testing a level of 2,500 points.
